draft.title: Effects of exclusion
card: Exclusion can harm a person's health. Stress, poorer access to care and a lack of support can all affect physical and mental wellbeing.
Exclusion can reduce income. A person shut out of work or training may earn less, which limits what they can afford.
Exclusion can weaken a sense of belonging. People left out of social life may feel isolated, unwelcome or unheard.
Effects can carry on across generations. A child in an excluded family may start with less money, fewer opportunities and less support than others.
draft.remember: Exclusion can harm health, income and belonging, and its effects can be passed on to children.

a.q: Which is an effect of exclusion described as a harm to a person's sense of belonging?
opts: Feeling isolated and unwelcome in the community
Earning less because of limited job options
Missing medical care because clinics are far away
Starting adult life with less family money
a.why: Feeling isolated and unwelcome is about belonging, which means feeling part of a group. The income and care options are real effects of exclusion, but they harm income and health, not belonging.
a.clue: Belonging is about how a person feels among others.

b.q: Tariq's parents were long shut out of steady work in their town. Tariq now struggles to find work too, as he had fewer resources and opportunities growing up. What does this show?
opts: Exclusion can carry on across generations
Exclusion only harms the person excluded
Exclusion harms belonging but not income
Exclusion always passes to the next generation
b.why: The parents' exclusion shaped the opportunities Tariq had, so the effects continued into the next generation. It is wrong to say it only harms the person excluded, because it reached Tariq. Effects can carry on, but the card does not say they always do.
b.clue: Look at who is affected besides the parents.

a.best: Feeling isolated and unwelcome in the community

b.best: Exclusion can carry on across generations

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('can'). Two distractors use absolutes ('only', 'always') and the third is plainly false, so a test-wise student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card, the remember line and question a are accurate and fit the point. In question b the right answer stands out as the only hedged option against absolute-word distractors, so the question is easy to guess.

b.q: Tariq's parents were shut out of steady work for years and felt unwelcome in their town. His mother's health suffered from the stress. Tariq grew up with less and now struggles to find work. Which detail shows effects carrying on across generations?
opts: Tariq struggling for work after a childhood with less
His parents being shut out of steady work for years
His mother's health suffering from the stress
His parents feeling unwelcome in their town
b.why: The parents' exclusion shaped what Tariq had growing up, and the harm now shows in his own working life, one generation later. The parents' lack of steady work is a real effect of exclusion, but it falls on the same generation that was excluded.
b.clue: Look for the detail about the next generation.
